messages:
anya: FYI getting multiple p99 pages for chat-completions in us-east-1, started ~08:12 UTC. Customers seeing timeouts.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-7689 — high-latency spikes on /v1/chat/completions — paging oncall.
jon: on it, grabbing traces and recent deploys. first guess: different model group is spiking, maybe kv cache pressure.
sre_shift: can you confirm model tags? I see a cluster of requests hitting `mistral-l` routes with 1.5x token lengths.
anya: yep, route=chat/mistral-l, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.2s, errors still low but timeouts creeping.
maya: rolling mitigation idea: temporarily raise p99 alert threshold for that route while we throttle long sequences + enable prefix cache warmup. avoids noisy pages for non-impactful blips. thoughts? :thinking_face:
jon: agree. Also propose adding a short debounce (5m) and require concurrent request rate > 50 before page — that should cut pages during small blips.
ops-rookie: how do we change thresholds quickly? Any one-liner?
jon: use `ops-alerts` CLI: ```ops-alerts update --route chat/mistral-l --metric p99_latency_ms --threshold 2500 --debounce 300 --condition 'concurrent_req > 50'```
sre_shift: make sure we document in the incident thread before changing. Also post a rollback plan.
anya: doing the change now, will also mute pager for that alert tier (5m). I'll run the CLI and attach output.
anya: (after) CLI: updated rule id=alerts-9837, old_threshold=1800 new_threshold=2500, debounce=300. Pager suppressed for 5m.
jon: can we also add a short-lived composite alert that requires both p99>2.5s AND backend_error_rate>0.5% so we only page on likely regressions?
maya: yes, add composite as a temp rule and tag as `incident-mitigation`. We'll remove after follow-up.
ops-rookie: creating a dashboard panel now: `dash: latency-per-route/mistral-l` with p50/p95/p99 + concurrent requests.
anya: good call — also pin traces filter: `trace.source:frontend AND route:mistral-l AND duration>1500` to speed triage.
sre_shift: initial customer impact: a handful of requests timed out but no widespread errors. Recommend noise-suppression for 30m, then re-evaluate.
jon: post-incident actions: 1) add per-model thresholds (not just per-route), 2) build model-length distribution alert to catch long sequence growth, 3) create runbook steps for changing alerts safely.
maya: I'll open follow-up tickets: ENGOPS-1421 (per-model p99 split), ENGOBS-1422 (dashboard + runbook), ENGRELIAB-1423 (kv-cache warmstart test).
anya: tagging oncall handoff: @sre_shift handing to @jon in 10m, will leave mitigation knobs in place until we confirm p99 back to normal for 20m.
jon: thanks. once p99 stays < 1.2s for 20m we'll revert thresholds and remove incident-mitigation rules.
sre_shift: noted. also add note to the postmortem about alert flapping — current rule caused noisy wakes for low-impact bursts. Need hysteresis more than raw thresholds.
anya: agreed. copying runbook fragment for the postmortem: ```- Confirm route/model causing p99 spikes
- If spike correlated with long sequences, throttle/limit seq length at gateway
- Temporarily increase p99 threshold + add debounce
- Add composite condition to require elevated error/concurrency
- Create dashboard slices for per-model and length distributions
- Revert changes after stable window and document rationale```
maya: nice. I'll link this thread in the incident ticket and schedule a 30-min follow-up sync. :calendar:
ops-rookie: one more nit: can we make the CLI command idempotent in the runbook? i.e. `ops-alerts upsert ...` so handoffs don't accidentally make multiple tiny changes.
jon: good idea — I'll update the runbook language.
anya: summary: mitigation applied (threshold raised to 2500ms + 5m debounce + composite rule added), monitoring dashboard created, handoff to jon, follow-up tickets opened. We'll revert after 20m stable.
infra-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied by anya at 08:18 UTC. Next update due 08:38 UTC.
jon: I'll post a revert note when I flip things back. closing oncall loop for now. :white_check_mark:
